thesis: Docusign's September 3 company-disclosed fiscal 2027 second-quarter results for the quarter ended July 31 reported revenue of $875.7 million, up 9%, IAM at 15.1% of ARR, GAAP gross margin of 79.7%, GAAP operating margin of 13.4%, and operating cash flow of $334.5 million while management raised full-year revenue and ARR guidance; this supports a long read. The strongest counter-evidence is $148.6 million of quarterly stock-based compensation and a 1.3 percentage-point foreign-exchange benefit to revenue growth; that does not overturn the read because IAM mix, GAAP margin, cash generation, and the raised outlook improved together. The active Mistwood patent case has September 18 pleading and joinder deadlines and a November 13 claim-construction-brief deadline, so active_litigation mechanically caps conviction at low; the current 10-Q identifies U.S. GAAP financial statements and does not report a qualifying recent governance-history event.
invalidation: IAM adoption fails to support total ARR growth, operating cash conversion deteriorates, or the scheduled patent proceedings reveal material exposure.
sources: Docusign fiscal 2027 Q2 release filed with the SEC: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1261333/000126133326000088/q227ex-991er.htm

thesis: UiPath's September 3 company-disclosed fiscal 2027 second-quarter results for the quarter ended July 31 reported revenue of $410 million, up 13%, ARR of $1.938 billion, up 12%, 109% dollar-based net retention, and GAAP operating income of $32 million, supporting a long read. The strongest counter-evidence is that ARR is an operating metric rather than U.S. GAAP revenue and net retention was only 109%; that does not overturn the read because the same quarter delivered double-digit U.S. GAAP revenue growth, positive GAAP operating income, and positive operating cash flow. The current U.S. GAAP 10-Q lists pending securities cases but no scheduled next-90-day ruling, hearing, trial, or compliance deadline, and the reviewed filing reports no fixed-set governance-history event.
invalidation: ARR or net retention weakens, U.S. GAAP operating profitability reverses, or disclosed customer adoption fails to translate into durable revenue and cash generation.

thesis: Vista Energy's September 8 issuer disclosure documented 66.8 MMboe of acquired proved reserves estimated as of December 31, 2025, after an acquisition that closed May 7; 26.1 MMboe are undeveloped. This is fresh documentation of acquired inventory, not a fresh organic discovery or evidence of current cash generation, so the 60-day rise does not yet support a new long thesis and the decision is avoid. The strongest positive counter-evidence is the enlarged 654.9 MMboe pro forma proved-reserve base, but it does not change the read without post-acquisition production, cash-after-capex, development-cost, and financing evidence. The reviewed issuer materials did not identify a scheduled next-90-day litigation event or a qualifying recent governance-history event.
invalidation: Fresh post-acquisition results demonstrate durable production growth, cash after capital spending, and financing economics that support incremental equity value.

thesis: The held BOXX position remains supported by the fund's disclosed role as an options-based alternative to an ultrashort-duration bond position and its current box-spread holdings. The near-52-week-high signal is mechanical short-rate carry rather than a breakout or company catalyst, so conviction is low. The strongest counter-evidence is the prospectus disclosure of counterparty, FLEX-options, valuation, cash-creation and authorized-participant risks; it does not currently overturn the holding thesis because the short-duration box-spread mandate remains intact and the September 10 fund page reported a one-cent 30-day median bid-ask spread. The reviewed current fund materials did not identify a fixed-set litigation or governance event.
invalidation: A confirmed adverse tax interpretation, material strategy or implementation change, persistent liquidity impairment, or repeated failure to track the stated short-duration objective after costs.
sources: Alpha Architect BOXX fund page and current holdings: https://funds.alphaarchitect.com/boxetf/

thesis: Tenable's September 10 company disclosure priced an upsized $725 million 0.25% convertible-note offering due 2031, with an additional $75 million purchaser option and expected September 15 closing; conversion may be settled partly in common shares. This fresh financing and dilution risk, alongside a negative 60-day price signal and 3.29x volume spike, does not support initiating a long, so the decision is avoid. The strongest positive counter-evidence is that part of the proceeds is intended for debt repayment and share repurchases and the initial conversion price carries a 40% premium; that does not remove the new capital-structure and potential dilution uncertainty. The reviewed issuer materials did not identify a qualifying recent governance-history event or scheduled next-90-day litigation event.
invalidation: The financing closes with clearly accretive debt reduction and limited effective dilution while recurring growth and GAAP profitability strengthen.

thesis: Kimco's 2.11x volume spike lacks a fresh company-specific catalyst in the reviewed issuer materials; the latest quarterly release instead showed a routine September 17 dividend payment, $2.7 billion of immediate liquidity, and unchanged transaction guidance. The signal therefore appears trading-flow or income-event driven rather than evidence of a new fundamental mispricing, so the decision is avoid at low conviction. The strongest positive counter-evidence is the 12% year-over-year dividend increase and ample liquidity, but those disclosed facts were already public in August and do not explain today's isolated volume confirmation. The U.S. GAAP annual filing and current 10-Q report effective controls and no litigation expected by management to have a material adverse effect, with no qualifying governance-history event identified.
invalidation: A fresh company disclosure ties the volume to durable same-property growth, accretive capital deployment, or a material balance-sheet improvement.

thesis: Qorvo's 33.21% 60-day rise and proximity to its 52-week high coincide with the pending Skyworks merger rather than a completed operating catalyst. Qorvo shareholders approved the transaction, but the current 10-Q says an FTC second request extended the waiting period and required regulatory approvals remain outstanding; this makes the move substantially event-mechanical and the decision is avoid at low conviction without a fresh merger-spread and closing-probability analysis. The strongest positive counter-evidence is shareholder approval and management's stated hope for a calendar-2026 close, but that does not resolve the regulatory condition or establish standalone upside. The reviewed filing did not identify a fixed-set governance-history event.
invalidation: Required regulatory approvals are completed and a fresh, source-backed merger-spread analysis shows favorable risk compensation, or standalone operating results establish a separate thesis.

thesis: BitMine's September 8 issuer release reported 5.93 million ETH, $593 million of cash and marketable securities, and a 99% quarter-to-date common-stock gain, while much of the narrative depends on management views about crypto prices, policy and investor flows. The 65.64% 60-day rise is therefore heavily crypto-beta and sentiment-driven rather than proof of recurring operating economics, so the decision is avoid at low conviction. The strongest positive counter-evidence is the large staked-ETH base and projected staking revenue, but those projections remain exposed to ETH price, staking yield, custody and concentration risk. The current U.S. GAAP 10-Q also says liquidity relied on equity financing and an ATM program, with a recent preferred-stock offering, which reinforces dilution and capital-formation risk; the reviewed sources did not identify a qualifying governance-history or scheduled litigation event.
invalidation: Audited results demonstrate durable per-share staking cash economics with reduced reliance on equity issuance and materially lower crypto concentration risk.
sources: BitMine September 8 release filed with the SEC: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1829311/000149315226041713/ex99-1.htm
